title: Welcome!
text:
I’m Jesse Peregrino.
I am a freelance researcher with expertise in survey development, data processing, and data visualization. You can learn more about me here.

title: About
text:
I am a freelance researcher and received a PhD in Psychology from the University of Texas at Austin in 2025.
During my PhD, my primary research was on people’s opinions on the origin of SARS-CoV-2. My recent publication demonstrated that groups of individuals have varying beliefs where the virus originated across 11 countries.
Much of my current interest has shifted problems with psychological measurement and how to improve our methodologies to better understand human attitudes and behavior.
I also use this space to host other works of interest. Feel free to reach out if you have questions or interest.

title: Brewing the lines: Charting Taiwan’s Tea Production
text:
I created a choropleth map of tea volume production for each region in Taiwan in 2023.
Technologies: R/RStudio, Inkscape, twmap package, and sf package
[Publication Source]

title: An island of tea produces surprisingly very little tea
text:
I wrote a post about the volume of agricultural production for 16 farm products in Taiwan from 1946 to 2024. The most defining graph was showcasing production change over time between 2015 to 2024.
Technologies: R/RStudio, Adobe Illustrator, Alluvial diagram
[Publication Source]

title: Weight Your Tea Bags
text:
I weighed the amount of tea leaves used in 13 different tea bags. Most of the leaves weigh 2 or 1.5 grams with some exceptions.
This is the first personal project to make data publicly available [see here]. I also spent more time incorporating open source icons and customizing the annotations to refine the visualization aspects.
Technologies: R/RStudio, Inkscape
[Publication Source]

title: A 23 year difference
text:
I compared the volume of tea production in Taiwan during 2000 and 2023. Three takeaways were:

Nantou County produces the most tea out of all other regions
The north parts of Taiwan used to produce a lot of tea
Most regions don’t produce as much compared to 2000

Technologies: R/RStudio, Inkscape, Slope Chart
[Publication Source]
